ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point A is any point on the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{7}{x}\left(x>0\right)$. Line segment $AB$ is parallel to the x-axis and intersects the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=-\frac{9}{x}$ at point B. Taking $AB$ as a side, a quadrilateral $\square ABCD$ is formed with points C and D on the x-axis. What is the area of $\square ABCD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw lines OA, OB, and extend AB to meet the y-axis at E, as shown in the diagram,\\
$\because$ AB$\parallel$x-axis,\\
$\therefore$ AB$\perp$y-axis,\\
$\therefore$ Area$_{\triangle OEA}=\frac{1}{2}\times7=\frac{7}{2}$, Area$_{\triangle OBE}=\frac{1}{2}\times9=\frac{9}{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ Area$_{\triangle OAB}=\frac{7}{2}+\frac{9}{2}=8$,\\
$\because$ The quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram,\\
$\therefore$ Area$_{\text{parallelogram ABCD}}=2\times$Area$_{\triangle OAB}=\boxed{16}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system. On the inverse proportional function curve in the first quadrant on the right side, point A is marked; on the inverse proportional function curve in the second quadrant on the left side, point B is marked. A and B are on the same horizontal line, so AB is parallel to the x-axis. Points C and D are on the x-axis, line segments BC and AD are the oblique sides, and figure ABCD appears as a parallelogram with AB as the upper base and CD on the x-axis. Reasoning: Let the common ordinate of the horizontal line segment AB be h, where h>0. Because A is on y=7/x, h=7/x_A, giving x_A=7/h. Because B is on y=-9/x, h=-9/x_B, giving x_B=-9/h. Therefore the length of AB is x_A-x_B=7/h-(-9/h)=16/h. From the figure it can be seen that ABCD is a parallelogram, the base AB is parallel to the x-axis, and C and D are on the x-axis, so the height of the parallelogram is h. The area is AB×height=(16/h)×h=16.
